evidence: The round-0 hunk of args.ts shows USAGE as a hand-written template literal while PROJECT.md claimed it 'is generated from the command table'. d9c807a made the claim true by deriving USAGE from FlagSpec/CommandSpec help rows, which was the first of the reviewer's two offered fixes.
guidance_note: Before writing a doc sentence that says a mechanism exists ('generated from the table'), grep for the mechanism and check it, or build it in the same commit.

evidence: The package.json hunk adds bin.miser -> src/cli/main.ts, and the d9c807a diff shows the shebang was missing until that commit. The agent added the shebang and exec bit and reports running ./src/cli/main.ts help directly.
guidance_note: When adding a package.json bin entry, exec the target file directly (not via bun run) before pushing.

evidence: COMMANDS was a plain object literal indexed by an untrusted string, so 'constructor' resolves through the prototype chain, and the agent reproduced the 'command.build is not a function' crash. Deriving Maps from the literals (d9c807a) closes both the command and flag holes without a guard at each lookup and keeps the Record type check.
guidance_note: When an object literal is looked up by user input, use a Map or a null-prototype table from the start.

evidence: This duplicates F1 on the same PROJECT.md line: USAGE was a literal that never read COMMANDS/FLAGS. The same d9c807a fix resolves it.
guidance_note: Before writing a doc sentence that says a mechanism exists, check that the code implements it.

evidence: This duplicates F2: the bin target had no shebang. d9c807a adds '#!/usr/bin/env bun' as line 1.
guidance_note: When adding a package.json bin entry, exec the target file directly before pushing.

evidence: The original USAGE said '--limit <n> keep at most this many, most recently modified first' for every command. On report, --limit rides to renderLimit after select()'s spawned-first and per-project narrowing. d9c807a puts the caveat on the report row of the generated usage text.
guidance_note: When a shared flag is consumed differently by one command, put that divergence in the user-facing help in the same change that creates it, not only in a code comment.

evidence: main.ts now calls select(picked, ...) with the scope-narrowed set, but select()'s criteria string still said 'of N discovered sessions'. d9c807a rewords it to 'in-scope sessions', and the agent shows a real run where 21 in-scope sessions had been labelled discovered while 493 were.
guidance_note: When a function's input changes from the whole corpus to a filtered subset, grep every label and count downstream that names that input ('discovered', 'total') and fix them together. That includes Selection.discovered and the masthead framing, which F12 later found.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: d9c807a never touched list.ts, and COLUMNS with its one-way satisfies check is original PR code. The reverse check is real hardening, not a live bug (the agent notes all 11 fields agree today), and 29eb1ee adds the Exclude witness and probes that it fails.
guidance_note: When a column array mirrors an interface, assert both directions of coverage at compile time when the array is first written.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the 'one place in this tool that touches the filesystem' claim was in main.ts and PROJECT.md from round 0, and d9c807a only added shebang lines above it. discover.ts does its own readdirSync/statSync. F1/F4's fix left the first half of that same PROJECT.md sentence unchecked.
guidance_note: When a review finding proves one clause of a doc sentence false, check every other claim in that sentence before you push the fix.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the unexported, untested main() with its two catch arms is original PR code shown in the hunk. 29eb1ee makes main take argv/Runtime and adds six exit-code tests through main.
guidance_note: When a module documents an exit-code contract, test it through the function that maps throws to codes, not only through run().

evidence: The behaviour change from a module-anchored to a CWD-relative out/ is real and was undocumented. 'Silently scatters' overstates it, because with a real bin a module-anchored path would write into node_modules. The agent took the reviewer's own 'document it' branch: 29eb1ee updates the help text and adds a DEFAULT_OUT test. The flag is a false positive because DEFAULT_OUT is original code.
guidance_note: When you replace a script with a bin, list each behaviour that changes (output paths, cwd assumptions) and state it in the usage text in that PR.

evidence: This is the same discovered-vs-in-scope gap F7 fixed in select()'s criteria string, here in Selection.discovered and framing(). The d9c807a fix reworded only the one string. The reviewer's 'discovered = picked.length' would have falsified selectionNote's 'found under the projects directory', so adding an inScope field (29eb1ee) was the better fix.
guidance_note: When fixing a mislabelled count caused by new scoping, sweep every place that consumes that count (Selection, masthead framing, notes) in the same fix.

evidence: The d9c807a test 'usage text lists every command and every option' loops over COMMAND_NAMES but over a hand-copied flag array. That reintroduces the drift F1's fix removed. The agent admits 'I introduced this hardcoded array in the previous round', and 5d4daeb exports FLAG_NAMES.
guidance_note: When a fix makes output derived from a table, have its test iterate the same table rather than a literal copy, and export the table's keys if needed.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 'out: d.out ?? DEFAULT_OUT' is unchanged from round 0, and an empty string passes ??. The agent confirmed --projects has the same hole and rejected empty values once in the parse loop for every flag. That is broader than the per-row check the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: When a flag parser checks for a missing value, also reject an empty value in the same place.

evidence: The original main.ts already ended with process.exit(main()), and 29eb1ee only reshaped its arguments, so this is not fix-caused. The agent measured piped output truncated at exactly 65536 bytes with jq failing, switched to process.exitCode, and added a real-pipe test that fails against the old code.
guidance_note: When a CLI's stated use case is piping (tool | jq), run that exact pipeline on a >64KB output before opening the PR.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: list/trace calling analyzeSession bare is round-0 code (hunk line 'picked.map((s) => listRow(analyzeSession(s, read)))'), while EXIT.FAILED promised to name the transcript. 5d4daeb routes all three commands through one naming() wrapper.
guidance_note: When a doc comment promises an error shape ('names the transcript'), check every call path that can produce that exit code.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: cell() replacing only tabs is original code, and 29eb1ee added only the MissingColumn witness above it. A newline in a directory name would split a TSV row, and 5d4daeb replaces [\t\r\n].
guidance_note: When sanitising a value for a line-and-delimiter format, strip both the field delimiter and the record delimiters.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: epochOf accepting anything Date.parse takes is original code. Non-date-only ISO strings parse in local time, which contradicts 'start of its day, UTC'. 5d4daeb enforces YYYY-MM-DD before parsing.
guidance_note: When a parser documents a specific input format, enforce that format with a pattern rather than handing raw input to a permissive library parser.

narrative: Round 0 raised seven real issues, with duplicates. The agent fixed each, often structurally: a generated USAGE, Maps instead of prototype-bearing literals. Most round-1 and round-2 findings carry ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags but target original PR code the earlier rounds simply had not flagged. Two are fix-related: F12 is the discovered-vs-in-scope gap F7's one-string fix did not sweep, and F13 is a hand-copied flag list in the test F1's fix added. Every round with a fix-caused finding also held independent findings, so no round was avoidable.
guidance_observations: Most of the PR's real defects (pipe truncation, empty --out, newline in TSV, local-time --since) were pre-existing edge cases the review surfaced only across rounds 1-2, so a pre-PR edge-case pass would have cut rounds.
The agent's different-fix choices on F3, F12 and F14 were each better than the reviewer's suggestion, and it said why in the thread.
Some fixes stayed narrow. F7 fixed one label but not the Selection count, and F1 was not checked against the rest of its sentence (F9).

evidence: The hunk shows rows accumulated in a loop and printed only after it, so a throw on session N drops the ids of 1..N-1 already posted. 6cd53e5 prints the header first and writes each row as its POST lands, and adds a fails-on-second test.
guidance_note: When a loop performs irreversible side effects, emit each item's record as it lands rather than batching output until the loop succeeds.

evidence: The hunk shows 'spans: spans.length' using a computed binding while scopeSpans calls flatten(...) again. The 6cd53e5 diff replaces it with 'spans,'.
guidance_note: After restructuring a function to introduce a binding, grep the function for the expression the binding replaced.

evidence: The test harness gained post/posts() with no otlp CLI test, which the agent concedes. 6cd53e5 adds six end-to-end otlp tests, visible in the diff.
guidance_note: When you extend a test harness with a new capability, write the test that uses it in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F2, the double flatten in domainExport, fixed by the same one-line change in 6cd53e5.
guidance_note: After restructuring a function to introduce a binding, grep for the expression the binding replaced.

evidence: 'check(subagents.length > 0 && stray.length === 0, ...)' fails every spawn-free session. The 6cd53e5 diff routes zero subagents through skip().
guidance_note: When a verification check is about a feature some inputs lack, route the absent case through the existing not-exercised path rather than into the pass condition.

evidence: 'const rootSpan = roots[0]!' follows a non-bailing check(roots.length === 1), so a rootless trace throws a TypeError. 6cd53e5 binds rootSpan from the same expression that checks the count and continues to the next domain.
guidance_note: When a script promises to collect every failure, don't use a non-null assertion after a check that only records failure; bind the value and skip the rest of the domain on failure.

evidence: This is the third report of the duplicated flatten in domainExport, fixed in 6cd53e5.
guidance_note: After restructuring a function to introduce a binding, grep for the expression the binding replaced.

evidence: No fixture made Math.min lower a call's tStart, so the detail.ts/billableOf split was untested. 6cd53e5 adds the EARLY fixture with a guard and two assertions on billableOf, and the agent reports that both mutations fail tests.
guidance_note: When a fix depends on a subtle invariant (billable instant != extent), add a fixture that makes the two values differ in the same commit.

evidence: PostResult.body was added for partialSuccess, but the loop checked only status. 6cd53e5 adds rejection() and throws on a non-zero rejectedSpans, with tests in both directions. The pushback reply-hint is wrong: the agent accepted.
guidance_note: When you add a field for a documented purpose, write the code that consumes it in the same change, or don't add the field.

evidence: The 503 test added in 6cd53e5 for F3 matches /rejected session [0-9a-f]{8}/. 'cli11111' is not hex, so the test passes only if the mtime ordering puts bbbb2222 first. 07a138e scopes the run with --session bbbb2222 and asserts the literal id.
guidance_note: When a new test asserts on 'whichever item fails first', scope it to one fixture or assert the literal id, so it never depends on sort order.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the ['list','trace','report'] loop and its 'every command' comment predate this PR, and the original otlp commit made them stale. 07a138e derives the loop from SCOPED instead of adding a fourth literal.
guidance_note: When adding a command, grep for literal lists of the existing commands ('list', 'trace', 'report') and comments that count them.

evidence: The hunk shows 'unexercised.length' counted raw while the list iterates a Set, and per-domain GROUPABLE skips already double-counted in round-0 code. The F5 fix's added skip only added another instance, so the finding is not fix-caused. 07a138e uses one Set for both count and list.
guidance_note: When printing a count above a deduplicated list, take both from the same collection.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: jaegerGet is round-0 code (not in the 6cd53e5 diff), and it retries every non-22 curl exit, so curl 7 is reported as 'truncated 5 times'. 07a138e separates connection-class exits 6/7/28 from the retry path.
guidance_note: When writing retry logic, list which failure codes are transient and retry only those; the default is fail fast.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the README line is original PR text, and it states the single tool-call-parent shape that verify-otlp.ts's own LEGAL_PARENTS comment says was disproved. 07a138e rewrites the line to the script's claim text.
guidance_note: When a check is corrected after real data disproves its assumption, grep the docs for the old assumption in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: d2b9ae4 touched only the README, and EXPORT_COLUMNS is original code lacking the reverse witness list.ts already had. The fix is right, but single-enforcer does not fit, since the change adds a second compile-time enforcer beside the runtime test. types-are-the-program, which the reviewer cited, is the apt law.
guidance_note: When creating a structure parallel to an existing one (EXPORT_COLUMNS beside list.ts COLUMNS), copy every invariant check the existing one carries.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 849cefe was README-only, and both 'Math.round(spend(detail.usage))' sites are original otlp.ts code. dd8e454 routes detailAttrs through ownTokens, and the agent verified identical Jaeger totals.
guidance_note: When one fact feeds two outputs (reported attribute and drawn width), compute it in one helper and call that helper from both.

evidence: EXIT.FAILED's comment 'names the transcript' was already false for the round-0 non-2xx throw. The F9 fix's partialSuccess throw added a second instance but did not create the drift, so caused_by is null. The agent took the reviewer's loosen-the-comment arm and explained why naming a healthy .jsonl would mislead.
guidance_note: When adding a new failure class under an existing exit code, reread that code's doc comment and update the contract it states.

evidence: scoped()'s docstring still enumerates 'all three commands' after otlp was added. That is the same hand-written enumeration F11's fix (07a138e) cured in the test file without sweeping main.ts. The agent concedes 'this docstring is the same hand-written enumeration that the same commit should have caught.'
guidance_note: When a finding exposes a stale hand-written enumeration of commands, grep the whole repo for that enumeration ('three commands', 'list, trace and report') before pushing the fix.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 5b34da1 only edited the EXIT.FAILED comment, and postJson's fetch with no signal is original code. 448b5f1 adds AbortSignal.timeout with a named message, verified against a never-answering server.
guidance_note: Give every outbound network call a bound when it is written, especially after measuring that the same backend stalls on reads.

evidence: This duplicates F19: the fetch in postJson is unbounded, original code, and was fixed in 448b5f1. The reviewer's point that verify-otlp.ts already documented this backend stalling is borne out by that file's header in the hunk.
guidance_note: When you harden one path against a measured backend failure (the GET retries), apply the same bound to every other path to that backend.

evidence: rejection(), added in 6cd53e5 for F9, has 'if (!Number.isFinite(rejected) || rejected === 0) return null;', which discards errorMessage on a warning-only partialSuccess, a case the OTLP spec defines. 448b5f1 returns a three-arm union and writes warnings to stderr, which is the reviewer's suggested behaviour.
guidance_note: When a fix starts reading a protocol field, read the spec for every state that field can carry, not just the one in the finding.

narrative: Round 0 raised nine real defects; three were the same duplicated flatten. The agent fixed all nine in 6cd53e5 with tests. Three later findings trace to fixes: F10 is a sort-order-dependent assertion in a test written for F3, F21 is a protocol state that F9's rejection() dropped, and F18 is the same stale 'three commands' enumeration F11's fix cured elsewhere. Most other flagged findings sit on original PR code that only gets flagged in later rounds. Every round with a fix-caused finding also had independent findings, so none was avoidable outright, and the PR hit the five-round review cap.
guidance_observations: The PR hit the reviewer's five-round cap, mostly from pre-existing defects (fetch timeout, curl retry codes, README shape claim, column witness) that each surfaced a round late. A pre-PR pass over network edges and docs would have saved rounds.
Fixes stayed local where a repo-wide grep was needed. F11's enumeration fix and F9's protocol-field fix each left a sibling instance that cost a later finding.
The agent verified fixes against reality (dead ports, a never-answering server, Jaeger totals), and no fix it verified that way drew a regression finding.
